# `Q-19-2` — Invalid Plot Document

> The file an image refers to is not a hephaestus plot document this version of Quarto can read.

## What this means

An image points at a file ending in `.hep`, Quarto read the file, but
it is not a hephaestus plot document Quarto can rebuild. The image is
left exactly as written and the rest of the page still renders; the
browser then shows a broken image where the plot should be.

The message includes the reason hephaestus gave for refusing the
file.

## Why this happens

- **It is not a plot document at all.** A file with the `.hep`
  extension that does not start with the hephaestus document magic —
  for example an empty file, or a download that returned an error
  page.
- **It was written by a newer library.** The document format version
  is compared for equality: a `.hep` written by a newer hephaestus
  (typically through a newer R plotting package) than the one this
  Quarto links cannot be read. The hint names the version Quarto
  reads.
- **It uses custom geoms or named formatters.** Those live in the
  program that wrote the document and cannot travel in the file, so
  the document cannot be rendered anywhere else.

## How to fix

If the file is not a plot document, regenerate it. If the versions
disagree, update Quarto to a release that reads the newer format (or
write the document with a matching library version). A document that
depends on custom geoms or formatters must be rendered by the program
that produced it — export a PNG or SVG from there instead.
